payload.text:
I read this as a request to perform a comprehensive, read-only code review of the App layer (and its orchestration of ClientCore/ServerCore) in EclipticRD - I will inspect the code against all six review dimensions and produce a rigorous findings report.

<verdict>FAIL</verdict>
<confidence>HIGH</confidence>
<summary>
The App layer features a well-crafted design system (`ERDTheme`), clean visual styling, and a modern macOS UI layout. However, it suffers from several major architectural issues: async race conditions in `ConnectionManager` state transitions, global input event leakage where overlay clicks are transmitted to remote hosts, resource retention of Metal renderers across sessions, singleton callback overwriting in `HomeView`, and dead/disconnected settings UI.
</summary>

<findings>
- [MAJOR] State Machine & Concurrency: Async race in `isUserDisconnect` causing spurious reconnection loops
  File: Sources/App/ConnectionManager.swift:135-151, 180-192
  Evidence: In `disconnect()`, `isUserDisconnect = true` is set, followed by `ClientCore.shared.stop()`. Inside `stop()`, `tcpChannel.stop()` calls `onDisconnect`, which triggers `ConnectionManager`'s callback containing an asynchronous `Task { @MainActor in ... }`. If the user immediately clicks "Connect" before this asynchronous `Task` executes on the MainActor, `connectBonjour` or `connectPIN` resets `isUserDisconnect = false`. When the previous disconnect's `Task` finally executes, it checks `if self.isUserDisconnect` (now `false`), and calls `self.attemptReconnect()`, triggering an unexpected automatic reconnection cycle for the old session.
  Suggestion: Track active connection session tokens/IDs or manage the disconnection state explicitly within structured tasks instead of relying on a mutable boolean flag across asynchronous `Task` boundaries.

- [MAJOR] Event Handling: Global `NSEvent` local monitor sends input events to remote host while interacting with SwiftUI overlays
  File: Sources/ClientCore/InputSender.swift:18-35, Sources/App/RemoteDesktopView.swift:39-65
  Evidence: `InputSender.startCapturing(in:)` installs an `NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents` matching all mouse and keyboard events window-wide. When a user expands `SessionControlsView` and clicks preset buttons, toggles audio, or types, `InputSender.handleEvent` converts the window coordinate to normalized view coordinates and sends mouse/keyboard packets over TCP to the remote host underneath the overlay.
  Suggestion: Check whether mouse event locations intersect overlay UI frames, or pause/filter input capture when interacting with session control panels or modal overlays.

- [MAJOR] Lifecycle & Leaks: `MetalRenderer` and `TrackingMTKView` retained past session disconnect
  File: Sources/ClientCore/ClientCore.swift:139-155, Sources/App/RemoteDesktopView.swift:1113-1129
  Evidence: `ClientCore.stop()` halts channels, ABR, audio, and decoders, but never clears `renderer: MetalRenderer?`. `MetalRenderer` retains `MTKView`, `MTLCommandQueue`, pipelines, and pixel buffers. Furthermore, `MetalViewRepresentable` does not implement `dismantleNSView(_:coordinator:)`, so Metal resources and view references persist in the `ClientCore.shared` singleton across sessions.
  Suggestion: Add `renderer = nil` in `ClientCore.stop()` and implement `dismantleNSView` in `MetalViewRepresentable` to release GPU render pipelines and view references.

- [MAJOR] Lifecycle & Concurrency: `HomeView.onDisappear` clears singleton `ServerCore.shared.onRunningChanged`
  File: Sources/App/HomeView.swift:48-56
  Evidence: In `HomeView.onAppear`, `ServerCore.shared.onRunningChanged` is assigned. In `HomeView.onDisappear` (which fires when switching to `RemoteDesktopView` upon client connection or navigating away), it explicitly executes `ServerCore.shared.onRunningChanged = nil`. If the host server stops, fails, or changes state in the background while the user is in a remote session or other view, state change notifications are lost.
  Suggestion: Use an `AsyncStream<Bool>` or a publisher on `ServerCore`, or coordinate `ServerCore` status through an observable manager rather than a single mutable closure property.

- [MAJOR] Error Handling & UX: `ServerCore.start()` fatal errors silently swallowed in `HomeView`
  File: Sources/App/HomeView.swift:201-209, Sources/HostCore/ServerCore.swift:76-80
  Evidence: In `ServerCore.start()`, if port binding fails (e.g. TCP 5900 or UDP 5901 in use), it catches the error, logs `[Server] Fatal error`, and sets `isRunning = false`. In `HomeView`, the "Start Hosting" button fires `Task { await ServerCore.shared.start(pin: serverPIN) }` without error handling. When binding fails, the UI silently reverts without providing any error alert, toast, or explanation to the user.
  Suggestion: Propagate throwing errors from `ServerCore.start()` to `HomeView` and present an error alert or banner explaining the failure.

- [MINOR] SwiftUI Correctness: Monolithic 1130-line `RemoteDesktopView.swift` combines unrelated responsibilities
  File: Sources/App/RemoteDesktopView.swift:1-1130
  Evidence: `RemoteDesktopView.swift` contains 1130 lines combining `NSViewRepresentable` bridges (`MetalViewRepresentable`, `WindowChromeInsetReader`, `SessionWindowReader`), AppKit subviews (`TrackingMTKView`, `SessionWindowReaderView`), keyboard event monitors (`KeyboardShortcutMonitor`), sparkline chart geometry calculations (`ERDSparklineView`), telemetry overlay (`StatsOverlayView`), and session controls (`SessionControlsView`).
  Suggestion: Break `RemoteDesktopView.swift` into focused modular files: `MetalViewRepresentable.swift`, `StatsOverlayView.swift`, `SessionControlsView.swift`, and `WindowBridgeViews.swift`.

- [MINOR] Consistency & Dead Code: Orphaned `ClientConnectView.swift` and duplicated `BonjourBrowserManager`
  File: Sources/App/ClientConnectView.swift:1-240, Sources/App/HomeView.swift:3-15
  Evidence: `ClientConnectView.swift` is never presented anywhere in the app (`HomeView` directly embeds host discovery and PIN cards). Additionally, `BonjourBrowserManager` in `ClientConnectView.swift` is an exact duplicate of `HomeBonjourBrowserManager` in `HomeView.swift`.
  Suggestion: Consolidate `BonjourBrowserManager` into a single shared `@MainActor` class and remove the unused `ClientConnectView.swift` file (or wire it up if intended as a modal sheet).

- [MINOR] Consistency & Dead Settings: "Preferred Video Codec" in `HomeView` settings is disconnected from encoder
  File: Sources/App/HomeView.swift:302-311, Sources/HostCore/ServerCore.swift:201-208
  Evidence: `HomeView` provides a segmented picker bound to `@AppStorage("preferredCodec")` ("HEVC" vs "H.264"). However, `preferredCodec` is never read in `ServerCore.swift` or `VideoEncoder.swift`—`VideoEncoder` always defaults to HEVC.
  Suggestion: Pass the `preferredCodec` setting into `makeVideoEncoder` in `ServerCore.swift` so user configuration is respected.

- [MINOR] UI Inconsistency: Telemetry sparkline labeled "FPS TREND (30S)" only holds 15 seconds of history
  File: Sources/App/RemoteDesktopView.swift:697, 755-760
  Evidence: `StatsOverlayView` samples at `0.5s` intervals (`Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 0.5)`). In `refreshStats()`, `fpsHistory` is capped at `30` samples. 30 samples × 0.5s = 15 seconds, but the UI header reads `"FPS TREND (30S)"`.
  Suggestion: Change history capacity to 60 samples for a 30s window, or update the header label to `"FPS TREND (15S)"`.

- [NITPICK] Consistency: App-level window minimum frame smaller than child views
  File: Sources/App/EclipticApp.swift:23, Sources/App/HomeView.swift:44, Sources/App/OnboardingView.swift:24
  Evidence: `EclipticApp` sets `.frame(minWidth: 450, minHeight: 400)` on the `WindowGroup`, whereas `HomeView` specifies `.frame(minWidth: 880, minHeight: 520)` and `OnboardingView` specifies `.frame(minWidth: 560, minHeight: 480)`.
  Suggestion: Harmonize the `WindowGroup` minimum frame to match `HomeView` (`880x520`).

- [NITPICK] Concurrency & Safety: Non-isolated work items in `ConnectionManager` mutating MainActor properties
  File: Sources/App/ConnectionManager.swift:313-338
  Evidence: `streamConfigTimeoutWorkItem` and `clipboardToastWorkItem` are scheduled via `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline:execute:)` using `DispatchWorkItem` closures that directly mutate `@MainActor` state rather than structured `Task.sleep` routines.
  Suggestion: Replace `DispatchWorkItem` timers with structured `Task` instances that can be cleanly cancelled and inherit `@MainActor` context.
</findings>

<solid_points>
- Design tokens in `AppTheme.swift` provide a consistent, cohesive dark-mode visual hierarchy with clean styling components (`ERDPanel`, `ERDRowCard`, `ERDStatusPill`, `ERDMetricTile`).
- Onboarding flow in `OnboardingView.swift` handles macOS Screen Recording and Accessibility TCC requirements cleanly, including the system-mandated app relaunch guidance.
- Window chrome insetting and fullscreen immersive mode handling (`WindowChromeInsetReader`, `SessionWindowReader`) integrate smoothly with AppKit window layers.
- Stream quality and resolution presets in `ConnectionManager` properly calculate aspect-ratio-preserved even dimensions for hardware video encoding.
</solid_points>

<blocking_issues>
- State machine race in `ConnectionManager` where asynchronous `onDisconnected` tasks interfere with subsequent connection attempts.
- Window-wide mouse and keyboard event leakage from `InputSender` during interactions with floating SwiftUI session controls.
- Retention of Metal rendering pipelines, MTKView, and buffers across sessions due to missing renderer cleanup in `ClientCore.stop()` and `MetalViewRepresentable`.
- Clearing `ServerCore.shared.onRunningChanged` in `HomeView.onDisappear`, severing host status observation.
- Silent swallowing of `ServerCore.start()` fatal port/network binding errors in `HomeView`.
</blocking_issues>
